```plato
//==
// # Optimization
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Optimization
//  - Constrained programs
//  - Optimization solver parameters

//==
// # Optimization
//
// The problem-independent vocabulary of numerical optimization: goals,
// stopping rules, results, and the brackets and outcomes of one-dimensional
// search. Parameter vectors are Array<Number> indexed by variable; optional
// limits use -1 for "no limit". Algorithm tuning and constrained programs
// follow in the sections below.

// Whether the objective is to be minimized or maximized.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_optimization)
type OptimizationGoal = Minimize | Maximize;

// Stopping rules for an iterative solver. Iteration stops when the step or
// objective change falls below AbsoluteTolerance, or below RelativeTolerance
// times the current magnitude, or when an iteration or evaluation budget is
// exhausted. A budget of -1 means no limit.
type ConvergenceCriteria
    implements IValue
{
    MaxIterations: Integer;
    AbsoluteTolerance: Number;
    RelativeTolerance: Number;
    MaxEvaluations: Integer;
}

// Why an iterative solver stopped.
type TerminationReason = Converged | MaxIterations | Stalled | Failed | NumericalError;

// The outcome of an optimization run: the best parameter vector found, its
// objective value, the iterations spent, and how the run ended.
type OptimizationResult
    implements IValue
{
    Parameters: Array<Number>;
    ObjectiveValue: Number;
    Iterations: Integer;
    Converged: Boolean;
    Reason: TerminationReason;
}

//==
// # Root finding and one-dimensional search

// An interval known to contain a root: the function changes sign between
// Lower and Upper.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisection_method)
type RootBracket
    implements IValue
{
    Lower: Number;
    Upper: Number;
}

// A triple bracketing a minimum: Lower < Middle < Upper with the function
// value at Middle below the value at both ends.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden-section_search)
type BracketedMinimum
    implements IValue
{
    Lower: Number;
    Middle: Number;
    Upper: Number;
}

// The outcome of a root-finding run. Residual is the function value at the
// reported Root.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root-finding_algorithm)
type RootFindResult
    implements IValue
{
    Root: Number;
    Iterations: Integer;
    Residual: Number;
    Converged: Boolean;
}

// The outcome of a least-squares fit: the fitted coefficients and the
// Euclidean norm of the residual vector at the solution.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Least_squares)
type LeastSquaresResult
    implements IValue
{
    Coefficients: Array<Number>;
    ResidualNorm: Number;
    Iterations: Integer;
    Converged: Boolean;
}

// The strategy for choosing a step length along a descent direction.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_search)
type LineSearch = FixedStep | Backtracking | WolfeConditions | GoldenSection | Exact;

//==
// # Constrained programs
//
// Optimization problems stated as matrices and bounds: linear and quadratic
// programs and the constraint relation they share. Rows of a constraint
// matrix are indexed by constraint, columns by variable; bounds run per
// variable. The goals, stopping rules, and results these problems are solved
// against live in the first section above.

// How a constraint row relates its left side to its right side.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constraint_(mathematics))
type ConstraintRelation = Equality | LessOrEqual | GreaterOrEqual;

// A linear program. Row i of ConstraintMatrix dotted with the variable
// vector relates to RightHandSide[i] by ConstraintRelations[i]; the objective is
// the dot product with ObjectiveCoefficients; LowerBounds and UpperBounds
// run per variable.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_programming)
type LinearProgram
    implements IValue
{
    ObjectiveCoefficients: Array<Number>;
    ConstraintMatrix: MatrixN;
    ConstraintRelations: Array<ConstraintRelation>;
    RightHandSide: Array<Number>;
    LowerBounds: Array<Number>;
    UpperBounds: Array<Number>;
}

// A quadratic program: minimize half of x' * Quadratic * x plus
// Linear . x, under the same constraint and bound conventions as
// LinearProgram. Quadratic is symmetric.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_programming)
type QuadraticProgram
    implements IValue
{
    Quadratic: MatrixN;
    Linear: Array<Number>;
    ConstraintMatrix: MatrixN;
    ConstraintRelations: Array<ConstraintRelation>;
    RightHandSide: Array<Number>;
    LowerBounds: Array<Number>;
    UpperBounds: Array<Number>;
}
```
